questions.stem: A food label states a biscuit contains 2 g of protein, 5 g of fat, and 15 g of carbohydrates. Protein and carbohydrates provide about 17 kJ/g, while fat provides about 37 kJ/g. What is the approximate energy content of the biscuit?
questions.explanation: Energy from protein: 2 x 17 = 34 kJ. Energy from fat: 5 x 37 = 185 kJ. Energy from carbohydrate: 15 x 17 = 255 kJ. Total = 34 + 185 + 255 = 474 kJ, approximately 470 kJ. Note that fat provides much more energy per gram than protein or carbohydrate.

questions.stem: In a calorimetry experiment, a student burns a crisp under a boiling tube containing 20 cm3 of water. The water temperature rises by 30 degrees C. How much energy was transferred to the water? (Specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J/g/degrees C)
questions.explanation: Energy = mass x specific heat capacity x temperature change = 20 g x 4.2 J/g/degrees C x 30 degrees C = 2520 J. Note: 1 cm3 of water = 1 g. This is the energy transferred to the water, but the actual energy in the food is higher because some heat is lost to the surroundings.

questions.stem: The calorimetry experiment described above gives a value lower than the actual energy content of the food. Why is this?

options.text: The food contains more water than expected
Heat energy is lost to the surroundings, not all transferred to the water
The water absorbs too much energy

questions.explanation: In a simple calorimetry experiment, significant heat energy is lost to the surrounding air, the boiling tube, and the clamp stand rather than being transferred to the water. Additionally, the food may not burn completely. These factors mean the measured value is always lower than the true energy content.

questions.stem: A person's basal metabolic rate (BMR) is the energy needed to maintain basic body functions at rest. Which person would have the highest BMR?
questions.explanation: BMR depends on body size, muscle mass, age, and sex. A large, muscular young man has the highest BMR because muscle tissue requires more energy to maintain than fat tissue, larger bodies have more cells requiring energy, and metabolic rate tends to decrease with age. BMR is measured at rest, so activity level does not affect it.

questions.stem: Two people eat the same diet. Person A exercises regularly; Person B does not. Person B gradually gains weight. Using the concept of energy balance, explain why.

options.text: Person B absorbs more nutrients from the same food
Person B's energy intake exceeds their energy expenditure, so excess energy is stored as fat
Person A's food is converted to muscle instead of fat
Person B has a higher metabolic rate

questions.explanation: Energy balance means energy input (food) should equal energy output (BMR + activity). Person A uses more energy through exercise, maintaining balance. Person B uses less energy, so their intake exceeds their expenditure. The excess energy is stored as body fat, leading to weight gain over time.
